body:
@LukasMasuch seems like a similar timing issue as https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7868?@dannyopts explanation is consistent with that issue as well.

I will note that importing a large module doesn't necessarily take a long time after the first import because Python will just keep it around in sys.modules, so I'm curious if that actually has any bearing on the effect occurring or not. I do think the st.navigation aspect might be important, since it conceivably introduces a little bit more head time for the page rerun to start up, giving the front end that much more time to process and send the second rerun before the number widget is reached in the first.

@Asaurus1 this bug is definitely only present for me when a large module is loaded. 

This is the sort of thing I was thinking could impact the timing - https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/aae0c64eea06e49fdb1cd1525ddc309b95796326/lib/streamlit/watcher/local_sources_watcher.py#L171 (in which case large is more about the number of modules that get loaded rather than the size in bytes).

@dannyopts if you replace the large module import with a time.sleep (or a for loop of a lot of little time sleep calls) does the problem persist? If so, then it's probably a timing issue. Unless there's another thread doing a bunch of dynamic imports, the set of modules in sys.modules shouldn't be changing after the program has run for a while.

No, as described above I couldn't reproduce the bug when the imports are replaced with `time.sleep` commands.

The `pypsa` library as an example takes about a second to import the first time, and on subsequent runs is much faster as it is cached in `sys.modules`. The bug occurs on subsequent runs, when the large pacakge has already been imported and is cached.

So, it seems it is a race condition that is affected by the state of `sys.modules`, but not directly related to executing the actual import the first time.

Although, I have just added a sleep in AppSession::_handle_scriptrunner_event_on_event_loop and it does cause the issue to occur much more frequently. I also commented the local_sources_watcher code and it seems to reduce the frequency of this bug but not remove it entirely 

```
time.sleep(0.5) # this change in _handle_scriptrunner_event_on_event_loop makes the bug happen much more frequently
if self._local_sources_watcher:
                    self._local_sources_watcher.update_watched_modules()
                    self._local_sources_watcher.update_watched_pages()
```

> @Asaurus1 no a sleep, nor a loop with mini sleeps, nor a busy loop replicate this issue.
> 
> I understand that the set of modules will not be changing, but my point was that this check itself will take some time, it must copy 2000 strings to a new set and then loop over those 2000 items and verify they are in the other set.
> 
That's a really good point! Yes it does seem like adding delays here has an effect on the frequency of the issue.
